| How often each maker wants the oil, brake fluid, plugs and filters changed is on the | scheduled maintenance | page, make by make. | To specification | Every oil change follows the maker’s specification for that car. | An engine in a BMW M car or a McLaren is built to close tolerances and runs hot. The maker tests and approves the oil it wants in that engine, and the rest of the job has its own rules too. At BMR Auto each oil change is done to the maker’s figures for the exact car and engine, from the oil to the last reset. | The oil approval | The approval code in the owner’s manual comes first. Two oils can share a viscosity on the label and still be built to different standards, so we match the approval the maker names for your engine. | The viscosity | Within that approval, the grade the maker allows for the engine, such as 0W-20, 0W-30, 5W-30 or 0W-40. A thinner oil is never used just because it is on the shelf. | The fill quantity | The engine is filled to the maker’s figure and then checked the way the maker says to check it, on the electronic oil level reading many BMWs use or on the dipstick. Dry-sump engines, used in many Lamborghini, Ferrari and McLaren cars, are filled and checked by the maker’s own procedure, often with the engine warm and running. | The filter | A new filter to the maker’s part for that engine. On cartridge filters the cap O-ring comes new with the filter, so the housing seals properly. | The drain plug and seals | A new drain plug seal or crush washer, and the plug tightened to the maker’s torque. Overtightening damages the pan threads, and a reused seal can weep. | The service reset | The service display is reset to the maker’s procedure, so the car records the oil service and counts down to the next one correctly. | Book an oil service. | Send the VIN and the mileage, and we quote the service with the oil your car calls for. | Book an oil service | Oil approvals | The oil approvals you will see on these cars. | Each maker publishes its own approvals, and an oil earns one only after the maker’s tests. Longlife-17 FE+ is a 0W-20 oil for selected gasoline engines and is not suitable for every BMW or M engine. Longlife-22 FE++ is a 0W-12 approved only for selected engines from 2022. | Mercedes-Benz and AMG | MB 229.5, MB 229.52, MB 229.71 | MB 229.5 and 229.52 cover grades such as 0W-40 and 5W-30. MB 229.71 is a low-viscosity approval led by 0W-20 oils, and it is not an upgrade for an engine that calls for 5W-30 or 5W-40. | Porsche | A40, C20, C30, C40, C40 GT | A40 is assigned to many Porsches through the 2020 model year. When your car needs an approval we do not stock, we order it before the appointment, so your engine gets the approval it calls for. | Tell us the year, the model and the VIN when you book, and we will confirm the oil your engine takes. Every make we service is on the | brands | page. | Request an oil change quote | Oil analysis | The oil that comes out tells us how the engine is doing. | Used oil carries traces of everything happening inside the engine. BMR Auto tests the oil it drains, in the shop or, when the car or the result calls for exact figures, at an outside oil analysis laboratory. The results go into the car’s record, so we can follow the engine’s condition from one oil change to the next and catch a problem while it is still small and inexpensive to fix. | Wear metals | Metals come off moving parts as they wear, measured in parts per million. | Motor Authority | gives aluminum from the pistons and iron from the crankshaft as examples. A rising figure points to the part that is wearing. | Coolant in the oil | Sodium and potassium are by-products of engine coolant. Finding them in the oil points to coolant getting where it should not, such as through a head gasket or an oil cooler. | Fuel in the oil | Fuel thins the oil and weakens its protection. Short trips and idling in traffic make it worse, and so can a leaking injector. | Dirt in the engine | Silicon in the oil suggests dirt or sand is getting in, often past a failing air filter or a leak in the intake. | The oil itself | Viscosity, water, soot and the breakdown of the oil from heat show whether the oil is still doing its job at the change, or whether the interval should be shorter. | Why the trend matters more than one result | Every engine has its own normal. The first sample sets a baseline for your car, and each sample after it shows whether a figure is holding steady or climbing. One high reading can come from a short interval or a recent repair. A figure that climbs over several oil changes is the one we act on, and it usually shows up well before a warning light or a noise. | In the shop and at the lab | At every change we look at the drained oil and the old filter for metal, sludge, coolant and the smell of fuel. When something looks wrong, when the engine has a known weak point, or when you want a full report, a sample goes to the laboratory and we go through the results with you. | Buying a car? Oil analysis can be part of a | pre-purchase inspection | . | In-depth inspection | Ask for an in-depth engine inspection with any oil change. | A dealer service visit is planned around a set time for each job, and an oil change is one of the shortest. When you ask for the in-depth inspection, BMR Auto gives your engine the time a careful owner would want it to have, and looks at it in far more detail than a quick service allows. | We do it because we have seen what it saves. A car that is looked after closely needs less repair work and costs less to keep. It also holds its value best, and a record of oil results and inspections is something a buyer will want to see when you sell. | If the inspection finds something, you get the findings and photos first, and a quote for any repair. Nothing is done without your approval. The car depends on several more, each with its own specification, and BMR Auto changes all of them to the fluid the maker names. | Transmission fluid | Many makers call the automatic transmission fluid a lifetime fill, which means there is no scheduled change in their plan. The fluid still ages with heat and miles. On BMW’s ZF 8-speed, specialists who cite ZF guidance recommend a change roughly every 8 years, sooner under heat and load; see | ZF 8-speed fluid | . | Dual-clutch gearboxes | An Ontario specialist reports that the wrong fluid in a McLaren SSG gearbox causes clutch judder and eventually clutch pack damage, and that skipped fluid service is the most common cause of early clutch wear on the Ferrari 458 gearbox. We use the fluid the maker specifies. | Differential and transfer case | BMW changes the rear differential fluid at about 50,000 miles on some models, and M cars get differential oil in their running-in service. The xDrive transfer case is a long-term fill in BMW’s plan, so we check its condition and change it when it is worn. | Coolant | BMW treats coolant as a long-term fluid, replaced only during repairs. Coolant still needs the right level and concentration, and we check both at every visit. | Brake fluid | Brake fluid draws in moisture over time even in a sealed system, which lowers its boiling point and corrodes the lines. Most makers set it by time as well as miles, and we change it with the fluid the maker names. Steps one national mobile service says it does not do are marked. | Booking and seller contact. You send us the VIN, the listing link and the seller’s name and phone. We contact the seller to arrange the inspection and ask whether the car can go on a lift and whether a test drive is allowed. Seller cooperation is the main limit on any inspection you cannot attend. | Paper checks. We run the VIN through NMVTIS and, for a Florida-titled car, the FLHSMV Motor Vehicle Information Check, and we read the service records and look up open recalls. Title brands, odometer history and theft records show up here before any tool touches the car. | VIN match. We compare the stamped VIN, the plate, the VIN stored in the control units and the records. A mismatch can point to a swapped module or a problem with the car’s identity. | Cold start. We start the car cold, before the seller has warmed it. A cold engine exposes cam adjuster rattle on the M157 AMG V8 and slow hydraulic pump priming on McLarens. | Full module scan, before anything is cleared. We scan the modules with dealer-level diagnostic software and save the stored and historic faults. A cleared fault memory hides the car’s history, and Porsche specialist guidance is to create the Vehicle Analysis Log before any fault is cleared. | Mileage cross-check. We compare the mileage stored in several modules with the cluster and the records. Odometer clocking has been reported even on Rolls-Royce Ghosts. A replaced or reset module can also cause a mismatch, so on its own a mismatch does not prove fraud. | Body and paint. We check panel gaps, glass dates and the paint, panel by panel, for signs of repair. This is where undisclosed accident damage shows. | Interior, electronics and flood signs. We test the switches, screens, roof and doors. Tire age is the last four digits of the DOT code, so 0308 means the third week of 2008, and the code may be on one side only. Some makers recommend replacing tires 6 to 10 years old whatever the tread, which matters most on low-mileage cars kept in warm, sunny places. One national mobile service says its inspectors may not lift the car or remove wheels. | Road test. Some faults and weeps appear only at temperature. | Further tests when the car warrants them. AAA, State Farm, Kelley Blue Book and Consumer Reports all give the same advice. If the engine was running when the car went into the water, State Farm says to switch it off as soon as it is safe and leave it off. | Photograph the waterline before anything moves. Insurers often send their own tow truck and may inspect the car by video, and Kelley Blue Book notes that starting the engine can hurt the claim. | Have it towed and keep it off the road. State Farm says not to drive a flooded car to test it. Salt water from a tidal or Intracoastal street makes the job more urgent, since State Farm treats salt water as an urgent electrical and corrosion problem. | Choose the shop yourself. Florida’s Chief Financial Officer says the owner has the right to choose the repair shop. It is common for insurers to keep lists of preferred shops. | A flooded hybrid or electric car needs its own first step. Water at one level has also reached every level below it. | Reference points for reading a waterline. Heights vary by model. Sources: AAA, State Farm, NRMA and BMW service bulletins. | Door sill. Water this high can reach the brakes and ABS and the fuel tank and fuel lines. State Farm says a mechanic may need to check the fuel tank and fuel lines for water before any attempt to run the car. Once water rises above the door openings, AAA says the car may need extensive disassembly to clean. | Seat base. The carpet and padding soak through and may have to come out, State Farm says, and AAA lists power seat motors among the parts that fail later. On many cars the airbag control module sits under the front seats, where flood water can cause a false deployment or a failure, according to Australia’s NRMA. On the BMW models in BMW service bulletins, the airbag module sits under the center console. | Bottom of the dash. AAA names control computers, sensors, wiring harnesses and connectors as especially prone to flood damage and hard to salvage. Heating and air conditioning parts and the small parts under the dash may work right after the flood and fail later. | Engine air intake. Water at the intake can be drawn into the cylinders once the engine turns, and that can destroy the engine. State Farm adds that floodwater can get into the fluids and the fuel system. | When you call | What happens when you call BMR Auto about a flooded car? | BMR Auto is an independent BMW, luxury and exotic car specialist at 325 W Dixie Highway, Dania Beach. | You call before the car moves. When your insurer is named and paying, the estimate goes to the insurer as well. Nothing is repaired until you approve it. | Modules | Can a water-damaged control module be repaired instead of replaced? | In a specialist’s case study on a BMW X5, rain water flooded the battery compartment and damaged the tailgate control module and the engine control module. Both were replaced with genuine BMW units, each coded and programmed to the car. | BMR Auto programs, codes, repairs and clones control modules for BMW, Rolls-Royce and Mini in the shop, so a replacement can be set up for your car here. See | programming and coding | . | The mail-in pages cover the BMW | footwell module | , the | FEM and BDC body modules | and the | DME engine computer | , each with the cars it fits and the price. These mail-in services repair module software and data, so call before you ship a module that has been in water. | KJ testing the battery and charging system on a BMW X5. | Did a module stop working after the water went down? | Tell us the car and what stopped working, and we tell you what the repair involves. | Call (954) 947-0057 | Faults that show later | My car seemed fine after the flood. Why is it failing now? | Parts on a water damaged car can work right after a flood and fail later from contamination by dirty water, AAA says, and corrosion can take weeks or even months to show unless every part is cleaned and dried. Kelley Blue Book points to the two to three months after a flood as when problems show up. | The parts AAA names include door locks, window regulators, power seat motors, heating and air conditioning parts and the small parts under the dash. | Read the faults before a part fails for good | A | diagnostic scan | reads the stored and historic faults in every module, so an intermittent electrical fault is on record before parts are replaced. A flooded car can also need | engine and transmission | work when water reached the fluids. | Call (954) 947-0057 | A Porsche Taycan in the shop. | Hybrids and EVs | Is a flooded hybrid or electric car safe to keep near the house? | NHTSA advises moving a flooded electric car at least 50 feet from buildings and other structures and contacting the dealer. A fire can sometimes start after the floodwater has gone down, InsideEVs reports. After Hurricane Ian, NHTSA research found that 3,000 to 5,000 electric cars flooded and about 600 were declared total losses. Of those, 36 caught fire. | State Farm says to stay away from the high-voltage parts unless you are trained, and to have a qualified technician inspect the car before it runs. | Call before you bring a flooded hybrid or electric car to the shop, and we tell you whether we can take it. Section 319.14(1)(b) of the Florida Statutes requires the brand in a conspicuous place on the title. | Not every state brands flood cars, so a flood car from another state can be sold in Florida with a clean title, FLHSMV warns. | A car repaired out of pocket may never carry a flood brand. | CARFAX estimated in October 2026 that about 75,000 water-damaged vehicles were on Florida roads, more than in any other state. | Not sure which shop should repair it? | You choose the shop. In a specialist’s case study on an X5, rain water in the battery compartment damaged the tailgate and engine control modules (see | modules | ). | Mini | Recall 23V-337 covers 2007 to 2013 Hardtop and 2008 to 2014 Clubman cars from road-salt states, whose footwell module in the driver’s footwell can short from water and salt corrosion. The fix includes checking the sunroof drains. Recall 24V-302 covers 2020 to 2024 Cooper SE cars whose high-voltage battery housing may not have been sealed properly. | Mercedes-Benz and AMG | Recall 22V-678 covers 2022 C 300 cars in which moisture in the trunk can leak into the rear SAM module and short it. Mercedes rescue guidelines list a risk of fire from a short circuit in a vehicle that is partly or fully submerged. | Porsche | The Taycan emergency response guide says to disable the high-voltage system after the car is recovered from water. Recall 23V-615 covered 2023 Taycans whose high-voltage battery may have too little sealant, which can let liquid collect inside it. The 911 driver’s manual places the 12-volt lithium battery under a cover in the luggage compartment. | Tesla | Tesla says not to operate a submerged car until an authorized shop has inspected it, and to tow it at least 50 feet from structures. Tesla bulletin SB-25-16-002 replaces the high-voltage battery flood port plungers on 2021 and 2022 Model S and Model X cars. | Land Rover and Range Rover | Land Rover publishes a wading depth for each model, 900 mm for the Range Rover and Range Rover Sport, and tells owners to look for signs of water ingress after a crossing. Recall 24V-023 covered water getting into the rearview camera of 2018 to 2022 Range Rover and Range Rover Sport, and 24V-364 brought a new fix for the Range Rover Sport. | Bentley | Bentley bulletin 2068829/3 covers water getting into the boot of the 2017 to 2025 Bentayga.
